Home Paid news feed Foto Agerpres Press Monitoring Bucharest Phone: +4 021.2076.110 Ministry of Finance approves allocation of 135.6 million lei to ensure continuity of ROMATSA services Category: English Date: 2026-08-28 18:26:04 Foto: Cristian Nistor / AGERPRES Photo The Ministry of Finance has approved the allocation of 135.622 million lei from the Government's budget reserve fund to supplement the budget of the Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure, ensuring that ROMATSA's operations and air navigation services can continue safely. According to a statement from the institution, the measure was approved by the Government on Friday and allows for the funding of expenses necessary to maintain operational safety, as well as personnel costs and other obligations arising from ROMATSA's operations and applicable legislation. 'The intervention became necessary because the resources collected through the EUROCONTROL mechanism—intended to fund the services provided by ROMATSA—had been temporarily rendered unavailable. ROMATSA provides air navigation services within Romanian airspace for both flights operating to and from the country's airports and aircraft in transit. The continuity of these services is essential for safe air traffic operations, and a temporary funding blockage cannot be allowed to compromise the functioning of such a service,' the Ministry of Finance explains. For passengers, this means that a temporary funding issue does not end up affecting flight operations. 'We are talking about a strategic service that must operate without interruption and under conditions of complete safety. The Ministry of Finance has approved this solution to ensure the continuity of ROMATSA's operations during a period of temporary unavailability of the resources due to it under the EUROCONTROL mechanism. At the same time, we have structured the mechanism so that the budgetary intervention is temporary: should these funds be recovered or subsequently transferred, they will be returned in full to the state budget. We thus ensure the functioning of an essential service without turning a temporary liquidity issue into a permanent cost for the budget,' stated Finance Minister Alexandru Nazare, as quoted in the press release. By approving this allocation, the Ministry of Finance ensures the necessary resources to prevent a temporary funding situation from affecting the continuity of a strategic public service and air traffic safety. The funds enable ROMATSA to continue its operations without interruption and to provide air navigation services for national and European traffic under normal conditions. The approved mechanism simultaneously protects the state budget. In the event of the subsequent recovery or remittance of amounts due via the EUROCONTROL mechanism, ROMATSA will fully reimburse the state budget for the funds received from the Reserve Fund. 'Thus, the allocation is temporary in nature and ensures the financial continuity of ROMATSA's operations, without permanently transferring obligations normally funded by EUROCONTROL resources to the state budget,' the statement notes. The Ministry of Finance gives assurances that it will continue to support the solutions necessary for the uninterrupted operation of strategic infrastructure and services, while maintaining budgetary discipline and protecting public resources. https://cointelegraph.com/news/us-offici.text: Written by Turner Wright staff writer Reviewed by Sam Bourgi staff writer Written by Turner Wright staff writer Reviewed by Sam Bourgi staff writer US officials work with CrowdStrike to fight malware behind crypto theft Latest News Published Sep 2, 2026 Federal authorities and private-sector partners were part of an operation to disrupt malware that redirected about $150,000 in crypto over the last eight years. Federal law enforcement officials, working with cybersecurity technology company CrowdStrike, announced action against entities behind malware that enabled the theft of $150,000 in cryptocurrency. In a Tuesday notice, the US Justice Department said it had disrupted the Sality botnet and malware in an international effort with Bulgarian, Hungarian and Romanian officials, as well as private sector partners CrowdStrike and the Shadowserver Foundation. US officials said that Sality was responsible for installing malware on compromised devices since 2003, resulting in crypto theft and cyberattacks. CrowdStrike reported that in the previous eight years, the entities behind Sality used EggJagger, a “clipjacking tool that monitors the clipboard for cryptocurrency wallet addresses and silently replaces them with addresses controlled by the operator,” to steal at least 12.1 million rubles, or about $150,000, in cryptocurrency. According to the company, the value of the “never-spent” digital assets peaked at about $1.5 million in January 2025. “When a victim copies a Bitcoin or Ethereum address to make a payment, the funds are redirected,” said CrowdStrike, explaining the technique behind the theft. According to CrowdStrike, the criminals behind Sality “lost the ability to communicate with infected machines” as a result of authorities’ efforts to disrupt the network. US officials and the company said Sality was used to steal crypto, while about 15,000 infected computers formed part of a peer-to-peer botnet that checked whether its systems were online every 40 minutes. https://www.dw.com/en/ukraine-and-russia.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5OiCf Ukrainian authorities have used drones to deliver food and medicine to residents stranded in the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky [FILE: September 12, 2026] Image: 34th Separate Marine Brigade "Borysfen"/Handout/REUTERS Advertisement Russia and Ukraine began a localized ceasefire early Tuesday to allow humanitarian aid into the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine. Both sides confirmed that the truce took effect at 3 a.m. local time (0100 GMT), following an agreement brokered by US first lady Melania Trump . Russia's Defense Ministry said its forces had stopped shelling in the Kherson sector to prepare for the humanitarian operation. Ukraine's human rights commissioner Dmytro Lubinets also confirmed that Kyiv was observing the agreement. "As head of the Ukrainian negotiating team, I confirm that the Ukrainian side is honoring its commitments," he wrote on Facebook. However, it could not be independently verified whether fighting had decreased. What is the humanitarian situation in Oleshky? Around 2,000 people, including up to 50 children, remain trapped in Oleshky, according to Ukrainian and US estimates. The town had about 24,000 residents before Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022 . The United Nations says residents face severe shortages of food and medicine. Mines and drone attacks have made it difficult for them to leave. International media have limited access to Oleshky, making it difficult to independently assess conditions in the town [FILE: September 22, 2026] Image: Ukrainian 34th Separate Marine Brigade "Borysfen"/AP Photo/picture alliance Former residents told news agency AFP earlier this year that people remaining in the town were starving, sometimes hunting pigeons or surviving on food grown in their gardens. "They've forgotten what bread is. You need flour for bread, and there's not even flour left," said Olga, who was in contact with two families still in Oleshky. Oleshky lies across the Dnipro River from the Ukrainian-controlled city of Kherson. Floodwaters submerged large parts of Oleshky in June 2023 after the collapse of the Kakhovka dam on the Dnipro River [FILE: June 10, 2023] Image: AP Photo/picture alliance Russian troops captured the town during the first days of the invasion in 2022. It suffered further destruction in June 2023 when the collapse of the Kakhovka dam caused widespread flooding. What role did Melania Trump play in the ceasefire? The White House said last week that Melania Trump had helped secure the agreement after holding talks with civilian negotiators from Russia and Ukraine. Her office said the first lady had also met United Nations officials who briefed her on conditions in Oleshky. Announcing the agreement on Friday, Trump said civilian officials from both countries would visit residents to assess their needs. US first lady Melania Trump has taken on an unusually prominent diplomatic role in efforts to address the humanitarian crisis in Ukraine [FILE: October 19, 2026] Image: Mark Schiefelbein/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance Doctors, food, drinking water and medicine are expected to reach the town before evacuation corridors are opened. "Residents who wish to evacuate will receive coordinated support and transportation to their preferred destination. I anticipate some will want to go to Russia, and some to Ukraine," Melania Trump said. Ukraine has accused Russia of preventing residents from leaving, an allegation Moscow denies. Neither side has provided details about who will monitor the ceasefire. Reports have also differed over its duration, with one account saying it could last through Saturday. What happened in Kyiv after the ceasefire began? Russian missile attacks continued elsewhere in Ukraine as the localized ceasefire began. Explosions shook Kyiv shortly after 3 a.m. local time Tuesday, according to witnesses, while air raid alerts sounded across several regions. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the attacks had damaged the Southern Bridge and associated subway infrastructure. City authorities said traffic on the bridge had been suspended. Buildings in Kyiv were damaged by Russian missile strikes, which also left several people dead or injured Image: Valentyn Ogirenko/REUTERS On Monday, a Russian missile attack on Kyiv killed at least one person and injured 10 others, including students at a dormitory. Further attacks caused casualties in Kharkiv and Pavlohrad. "It is important that the world sees that Russia is showing nothing but a desire to kill and continue waging war," Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy wrote after the attacks. Could the Oleshky ceasefire help revive Ukraine peace talks? The limited truce in Oleshky comes ahead of another round of US-mediated peace talks between Washington, Moscow and Kyiv, expected in November. Negotiations have been effectively frozen since the United States and Israel launched joint strikes on Iran in February. The last trilateral peace talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US took place in Geneva in February 2026, ending without a breakthrough [FILE: February 17, 2026] Image: Yekaterina Chesnokova/ITAR-TASS/IMAGO Previous attempts to establish ceasefires have repeatedly failed amid deep mistrust between Russia and Ukraine. More than four and a half years after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, hundreds of thousands of soldiers and civilians have been killed, while millions have been forced to flee their homes. https://business-review.eu/sustainabilit.text: PepsiCo Romania commits over EUR 550,000 to community development initiatives through 2028 PepsiCo Romania is redirecting over €550,000 from its corporate income tax to five civil society and academic organizations to support projects that will be implemented between 2026 and 2028. These initiatives focus on expanding access to education for children and young people from vulnerable backgrounds, developing technical skills, preparing the next generation of farmers, and improving access to water in rural communities across Romania. The projects implemented by the beneficiary organizations address areas that also align with pep+ (PepsiCo Positive), the company’s end-to-end strategic transformation that puts sustainability at the center of its business model and aims to build a stronger, more resilient future for PepsiCo and the communities where it operates. “Through these partnerships, we continue to contribute to the sustainable development of the communities we are part of. We support access to quality education and professional development opportunities for young people, help prepare future generations of specialists and leaders in industry and agriculture, and stand alongside rural communities facing challenges related to water access. The expertise of our partner organizations is essential in ensuring that these initiatives create tangible, lasting change for the communities they serve,” said Mihaela Hristea, General Manager, PepsiCo East Balkans. Education and opportunities for the future The National University of Science and Technology POLITEHNICA Bucharest, with support from PepsiCo Romania, is launching Technical Future Academy, an initiative that marks a new stage in the collaboration between the two organizations and builds on the experience of the Campus PepsiCo program. The initiative aims to increase students’ interest in industrial fields, support the development of professional skills, and facilitate the transition from academia to the workforce. Read more about Lenovo AI Express with NVIDIA accelerates path to Hybrid AI Factory in weeks read more At the same time, PepsiCo Romania continues its partnership with World Vision Romania, first established in 2021, through the “I Want to Attend 9th Grade” program, which helps students from vulnerable backgrounds continue their education in high school. Through financial, educational, and psychosocial support, as well as the provision of hot meals, the initiative helps reduce the risk of school dropout. The company is also continuing its collaboration, launched five years ago, with Casa Bună Association, helping facilitate access to education for children from vulnerable communities through integrated educational support and personal development programs delivered in a safe and stable environment. Developing leaders and entrepreneurs in Romanian agriculture Agriculture plays an important role in the development of Romania’s rural communities. To help prepare the next generation of farmers and entrepreneurs, PepsiCo Romania supports members of the farming community through the “Young Leaders for Agriculture” and “Entrepreneur in Agriculture 4.0” programs run by the Romanian Farmers’ Club for High-Performance Agriculture. These initiatives foster leadership, management, and entrepreneurial skills while contributing to the competitiveness of Romanian agriculture. Solutions for water access and rural community resilience Water is an essential resource for rural communities and agriculture. That is why PepsiCo Romania supports the “Water Is Identity. Daia and Cernat” program, implemented by the Human Made Art Association, which aims to improve access to water and restore ecosystems in Harghita and Covasna counties. In the village of Daia, Harghita County, activities include building water-retention structures using locally available natural materials, planting trees to support these efforts, and creating a demonstration garden that serves as a best-practice example for rainwater harvesting. In Cernat, Covasna County, activities include cleaning the canal that supplies the local watermills and organizing educational programs for children and young people to help preserve local heritage and traditions.
